specification.intent: Answer AI-chat messages through a local provider and document-search tool with durable bounded execution and authorized attachments.

requirements.title: Durable AI bot
requirements.description: Persist bot runs, enforce one active run per source message, use authorized RAG search, bound retries/timeouts and optionally attach a permitted file_id.

specification.goal: A reviewed, deterministic implementation plan for stage 9.
constraints: Stage 6 chat/file/message and stage 8 RAG contracts are consumed.
Provider/model names are configurable and local by default.
No cloud fallback or unbounded retries.
No frontend, central router or WS-hub writes.

leadOwned.reason: The controller owns frozen plan-package artifacts retained in the implementation delta.
The controller maintains the repository progress log for this implementation package.

workstreams.title: Durable AI bot
workstreams.launchGate: Stages 5, 6 and 8 are accepted in origin/dev at the exact declared base SHA (dev@e33c6997d73faf687a711105e82c77cabee172bb, which carries the completed backend contour and the stage 2-4/7 frontend contour through PRs #16-#21); create feature/2026-09-28-backend-bot from dev@e33c6997d73faf687a711105e82c77cabee172bb.
workstreams.qualityFloor: Duplicate delivery cannot create two active runs and no unauthorized document/file enters a response.

criteria.title: Durable bot response
criteria.statement: One AI message creates at most one active bot run and a bounded response; retries and provider timeout are explicit.
criteria.description: Run state is durable and idempotent.

criteria.title: Bot authorization and provider boundary
criteria.statement: Search and optional attachment remain authorized to the source chat/user, with no cloud fallback or prompt scope escape.
criteria.description: The bot cannot widen RAG or file scope.

evidence.description: Idempotency, retry, timeout and durable run unit/integration receipt.

acceptance.releaseGate: Deterministic durable-run and authorization evidence passes; Ollama status is explicit.
acceptance.qualityFloor: No criterion is accepted from prose alone.

commands: (cd backend && PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/unit/bot tests/integration/bot)

releaseTarget.environment: local-only Docker Compose backend plus a native Ollama chat endpoint (url/model configurable, default model qwen3:14b per the master plan); the deterministic gate runs on sqlite with injected fake providers

releaseImpact: Adds a durable local AI bot behind the owned backend; no cloud or production promotion is claimed.
finalAuditGates: [AC-BOT-2|EV-BOT-2] bot authorization and provider boundary pass

securityGates.statement: Search and attachments are authorized to the source chat/user.
Provider and prompt scope are local/configurable with no cloud fallback.

chat/file/message/RAG/WS-hub/central router ownership remains with predecessor stages

compatibility.chatContract: Chat.is_ai (stage 6) gates bot answering; ChatService.require_member authorizes the requester and ChatService.add_member joins the bot user with the requesting member as requester
compatibility.messageContract: the bot answer is posted through MessageService.create as the bot user; membership and file authorization (chat-owned, status ready) are enforced by the consumed service and never bypassed; answer content is capped to fit MessageCreate limits
compatibility.ragContract: DocumentService.search is consumed behind an injectable seam; retrieval stays chat-scoped, ready-only and file_id-traceable exactly as accepted in stage 8
compatibility.provider: local Ollama /api/chat behind a provider protocol (url, model, timeout configurable; default model qwen3:14b); malformed payloads, HTTP and transport failures are explicit provider errors; no cloud fallback and no langchain - plain httpx keeps the dependency set unchanged (backend/pyproject.toml untouched)
compatibility.botSettings: backend/app/bot/config.py reads CHATTY_BOT_* env settings with safe defaults (provider url/model, timeout, max attempts, bot user email, rag top-k, answer cap); backend/app/core/config.py is untouched
compatibility.endpointMounting: the bot router registers through the stage-5 seam app.api.v1.router.register_domain_router, called from backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/__init__.py; main.py and router.py stay untouched
compatibility.botIdentity: the bot user is resolved by configured email (CHATTY_BOT_USER_EMAIL, default bot@chatty.local) and is a normal account created through the public auth API by the operator - no seeding code is added; until the account exists, runs fail explicitly with bot_user_not_configured (the accepted steady state, recorded in EV-BOT-2); the stage-5 user model gains no is_bot column and the bot joins only is_ai chats server-side
compatibility.trigger: runs are created by a synchronous bounded REST call (POST /chats/{chat_id}/bot/runs with the source message id); the WS-hub auto-trigger and live broadcast of bot answers are an explicit AI-UI carry-forward
compatibility.sourceMessage: the run validates its source message before any external call: it must exist (404 message_not_found), belong to the route chat (400 message_not_in_chat, mirroring the history cursor check in MessageService), carry text content (400 message_content_required for file-only sources - the RAG query needs text) and not be authored by the bot user itself (409 bot_own_message); cross-chat message ids therefore cannot pull foreign content into a chat's answer
compatibility.retries: execution claims are conditional queued-to-running compare-and-set updates; the concurrent first delivery resolves through the unique(message_id) IntegrityError path exactly like MessageService.create; duplicate delivery against a fresh, running or succeeded row returns the existing run without re-execution; a queued/running row older than CHATTY_BOT_STALE_AFTER_SECONDS (default 180; the service takes an injectable clock so tests are deterministic) may be re-claimed with attempt++; attempts are bounded per run by CHATTY_BOT_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 2) and an exhausted budget is an explicit 409 retry_budget_exhausted - never a silent loop
compatibility.runForeignKeys: bot_runs.message_id references messages ON DELETE CASCADE (a run dies with its source message, both under the chat's own CASCADE), bot_user_id ON DELETE RESTRICT, response_message_id and attachment_file_id ON DELETE SET NULL
